suggestions: Consider adding specific PBS streamline codes for sertraline (2622B) and escitalopram (8847M) in explanation for traceability
Depression MCQs could benefit from mentioning monitoring requirements (review at 2 weeks for side effects, 4-6 weeks for efficacy)
Postpartum depression MCQ could explicitly state sertraline is TGA Pregnancy Category C but compatible with breastfeeding per eTG
strengths: All psychiatric medications use correct Australian terminology - no American drug names detected
SSRI selection appropriate (sertraline, escitalopam) matching eTG Psychiatry first-line recommendations
Correct Australian dosing for elderly depression (sertraline 25mg - half usual starting dose)
Appropriate recognition of treatment-resistant depression pathway (2 SSRI failures → SNRI/augmentation)
Lithium monitoring frequencies match Australian guidelines (3-monthly levels, 6-monthly UEC/TFTs)
Valproate contraindication in women of childbearing age correctly stated (TGA 2018 restriction)
Benzodiazepine warnings appropriate (dependence risk, avoid long-term use)
Clozapine monitoring schedule matches TGA mandated requirements (weekly → fortnightly → monthly FBC)
Acute dystonia management correct (benztropine IM) - Australian emergency protocol
Alcohol withdrawal protocol correct (diazepam + thiamine 300mg IV before glucose)

violations.description: Multiple MCQs (PSY-SUICIDE-MHA series) lack complete SAFE-T assessment in explanations - only risk stratification mentioned without explicit documentation of all 5 SAFE-T elements (Specific plan, Access to means, Feelings, Earlier attempts, Threat)
Cultural safety elements (Aboriginal/TSI status, SEWB framework, Aboriginal liaison) not explicitly mentioned in any MCQ explanations - missed opportunity for culturally safe psychiatry education
Generic brand names used appropriately (sertraline, olanzapine, quetiapine) but some explanations lack specific Australian dosing references (e.g., PBS restrictions, TGA guidelines)

suggestions: Add explicit SAFE-T framework assessment breakdown in suicide risk MCQ explanations (currently only SAD PERSONS mentioned)
Include Aboriginal/TSI cultural safety considerations in at least 2-3 representative MCQs (e.g., depression, psychosis, suicide risk scenarios)
Add Australian-specific crisis contacts in EVERY suicide-related MCQ (Lifeline 13 11 14, Beyond Blue 1300 224 636, Aboriginal crisis line 13YARN 13 92 76)
Specify PBS restrictions for medications where relevant (e.g., clozapine authority script)
Include Mental Health Act state-specific differences more explicitly (NSW vs VIC vs QLD criteria)
strengths: Comprehensive coverage of emergency psychiatry topics (depression, anxiety, bipolar, psychosis, suicide risk, substance use)
Mental Health Act involuntary criteria correctly applied in acute mania and suicide risk scenarios
Australian medication names used consistently (sertraline, venlafaxine, quetiapine - NOT US brand names)
Clozapine monitoring schedule accurate (weekly FBC 18wk → fortnightly 52wk → monthly)
Suicide risk stratification present in multiple MCQs (high/medium/low with appropriate interventions)
De-escalation techniques and least restrictive principle appropriately emphasized
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome, and extrapyramidal side effects correctly differentiated
agent_evaluations.notes: Dataset contains 100 psychiatry MCQs with reasonable clinical accuracy and Australian context. Key areas for improvement: (1) Explicit SAFE-T framework documentation in suicide risk questions, (2) Aboriginal/TSI cultural safety integration, (3) More specific Australian crisis contacts. Manual review recommended for questions PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-334, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-562, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-967 to verify complete suicide risk assessment coverage.
